requests.what: A drill hall on the combined campus -- the largest indoor space on the base, big enough for an entire intake at once.
requests.why: Blocks Assembly (episode-c1e1--assembly), which needs rows of chairs, a raised platform and the framed charter above it. Long Hall is the mess (2,614 m2) and is already the Canteen scene's building; a base this size would plausibly drill somewhere else, but if you would rather the mess double as the assembly space, say so and I will site it there instead.
requests.hint: The fortress island -- Landing End, near Long Hall and the Intake Infirmary, where the intake already lives and eats. CORRECTED 2026-09-22 after Ingram: "It has to be on the 'Port Island' island... That's the military base... The shore and the mainland aren't for the Directorate military to define."
requests.resolution: the-drill-hall (D4.94, Island Centre, 7,246 m2 single span) -- drawn by Ingram 2026-09-22, adopted at scene depth.

requests.what: The administrative block -- offices on the lower floors, a carpeted top floor with the senior staff on it.
requests.why: Blocks TWO scenes. As Discussed (episode-c1e2--as-discussed) is the Section Officer's own office: small, tidy, duty roster on the wall, in-tray and out-tray. The Hammer (episode-c1e2--the-hammer) is the top floor of the same building -- 'Carpet, which none of them has stood on since they arrived', and a closed door with a bench outside it. Nothing in the gazetteer is the base's admin block; the Goods Office and Permit Office are both single-purpose civic buildings.
requests.hint: The fortress island -- Island Centre, the Directorate's own downtown: 'offices, canteens and billets on a rectilinear grid laid out all at once'. That is where a carpeted top floor with senior staff on it belongs, rather than out among the candidate rows. CORRECTED 2026-09-22 after Ingram: "It has to be on the 'Port Island' island... That's the military base... The shore and the mainland aren't for the Directorate military to define."
requests.resolution: the-administrative-block (E4.06, Island Centre, 6 storeys) -- adopted at scene depth, serving both As Discussed and The Hammer. Ingram drew a second admin building alongside it, adopted as the-establishment-offices at sketch depth (no scene casts it yet).

requests.what: The muster yard, with the duty board under its tin hood outside a Time Office hatch.
requests.why: Blocks TWO scenes. The Board (episode-c1e2--the-board) is mid-morning at the duty board -- wooden slot-tiles being taken down and put back. The Override (episode-c1e2--the-override) is evening muster in the same yard under the same board. The Haulage Yard is a hard yard but belongs to the works' lorries, and The Time Office is over in Island Centre, not on the base. The yard clock also matters: The Long Afternoon names it as the thing evening muster is measured against.
requests.hint: The fortress island -- The Garrison, 'the working half of the base: workshops, the magazine, and the gatehouse that decides who gets through'. A muster yard with a duty board and a Time Office hatch is a working-half object, not a downtown one. CORRECTED 2026-09-22 after Ingram: "It has to be on the 'Port Island' island... That's the military base... The shore and the mainland aren't for the Directorate military to define."
requests.resolution: the-muster-yard (D3.28, The Landing End, 5,430 m2, 372 m from the Main Mech Hangar) -- adopted at scene depth, serving both The Board and The Override.

requests.what: The outer sea wall on the fortress island's seaward side, east end, below the garrison yard -- reachable on foot only around low water.
requests.why: Blocks Slack Water (episode-c1e2--slack-water), a 35-45 minute scene whose whole premise is the tide: 'reachable on foot for about four hours either side of low water, and not at all otherwise', with a hard horizontal weed line at head height running the length of the wall. There is no sea wall anywhere in the gazetteer.
requests.hint: The fortress island's OWN outer edge -- the seaward side below the garrison, facing the East Basins or the outer channel. Explicitly NOT the mainland shore: my first hint said 'eastern shore' and that was the error. CORRECTED 2026-09-22 after Ingram: "It has to be on the 'Port Island' island... That's the military base... The shore and the mainland aren't for the Directorate military to define."
requests.resolution: the-outer-sea-wall (E3.07, The Long Sheds, point) -- adopted at scene depth. Sited on the island's own north-east seaward side, NOT the mainland shore.

requests.what: Manako's tea house, in a particular district of the city where he has a lot of influence.
requests.why: Blocks The Errand (episode-c1e1--the-errand), where the party meets Manako. Ingram, 2026-09-27 (LEDGER #46): "Manako's tea house and the technical workshop both need placing and I don't know that I'm 100% confident where either of them are. These both need to be placed / review in the gazetteer before they are considered done. Manako's tea house needs to be a particular district in town, somewhere he has a lot of influence." The scene currently points at the-tea-house-420, which is up for review.
requests.hint: A district of the city (not the Directorate's island) where an old man can be quietly important: locals and the tea house's staff defer to him without making a show of it. Review the-tea-house-420 and move or replace it.

requests.what: A technical workshop, an instrument makers', a few streets from Manako's tea house: the first place The Errand's docket sends the party.
requests.why: Blocks The Errand. Ingram, 2026-09-27 (LEDGER #45, #46): the party goes first to a more technical workshop whose people can't help and send them on to Manako; it must be "closer than 600m, ideally just a few streets away" from the tea house. Claude's first pick, the Instrument Shop on the works, was about 600 m away and is withdrawn.
requests.hint: Place it after req-5, a few streets from wherever the tea house lands. A small workshop with long benches and a counter; it makes gauges and spirit levels.
